templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. Some [B] are [C].
3. All [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [A] are [D].
Conclusion II: Some [B] are [D].
Which follows?
templates.explanation: Some B are C + All C are D → Some B are D (Conclusion II valid). Some A are B + Some B are D → cannot conclude Some A are D. Only Conclusion II follows.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. Some [B] are not [C].
3. All [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [A] are not [C].
Conclusion II: Some [D] are [B].
Which follows?
templates.explanation: All C are D → Some D are C (conversion). Some B are C → Some B are D. Conclusion II valid. Conclusion I: Some B are not C doesn't mean Some A are not C (A may be entirely in C). Conclusion I not valid.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. All [B] are [C].
3. No [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: No [A] are [D].
Conclusion II: No [B] are [D].
Conclusion III: Some [C] are [A].
Which all follow?
templates.explanation: All A→B→C + No C are D → No A are D (I valid), No B are D (II valid). All A are C → Some C are A (III valid by conversion). All three follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. All [B] are [C].
3. No [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: No [B] are [D].
Conclusion II: Some [A] are not [D].
Conclusion III: All [C] are [B].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: All B are C + No C are D → No B are D (I valid). Some A are B + No B are D → Some A are not D (II valid). Conclusion III reverses All B are C → not valid. I and II follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. No [A] are [B].
2. Some [B] are [C].
3. All [C] are [A].
Conclusion I: Some [C] are not [B]... wait — is there any contradiction in the statements?
templates.explanation: No A are B (stmt 1) + All C are A (stmt 3) → No C are B. But stmt 2 says Some B are C → contradiction. The statements are Inconsistent/Contradictory.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. No [B] are [C].
Conclusion I: Some [A] are not [C].
Conclusion II: Some [C] are not [A].
Conclusion III: No [A] are [C].
Which follows?
templates.explanation: Some A are B + No B are C → Some A (those that are B) are not C → Conclusion I valid. Conclusion II and III cannot be determined. Only Conclusion I follows.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. Some [A] are [C].
3. No [B] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [C] are [B].
Conclusion II: No [A] are [D].
Conclusion III: Some [C] are not [D].
Which all follow?
templates.explanation: Some A are C + All A are B → Some C are B (I valid). All A are B + No B are D → No A are D (II valid). Some C are B (from I) + No B are D → Some C are not D (III valid). All three follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. No [C] are [B].
3. Some [D] are [C].
Conclusion I: No [A] are [C].
Conclusion II: Some [D] are not [B].
Conclusion III: All [D] are [A].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: All A are B + No C are B → No C are A → No A are C (I valid). Some D are C + No C are B → Some D are not B (II valid). III is not supported. I and II follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. All [B] are [C].
3. Some [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [A] are [C].
Conclusion II: Some [D] are [B].
Conclusion III: All [C] are [D].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: Some A are B + All B are C → Some A are C (I valid). Some C are D does NOT mean Some D are B (II not valid). III is too strong. Only Conclusion I follows.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. All [B] are [C].
3. Some [D] are [A].
Conclusion I: Some [D] are [C].
Conclusion II: Some [D] are [B].
Conclusion III: All [D] are [B].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: Some D are A + All A are B → Some D are B (II valid). Some D are B + All B are C → Some D are C (I valid). III is too strong (All D are B not established). I and II follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. No [A] are [C].
Conclusion I: Some [B] are not [C].
Conclusion II: No [B] are [C].
Is it a complementary pair (one must be true)?
templates.explanation: Some A are B + No A are C → those A that are B are not C → Some B are not C (I valid). Conclusion II (No B are C) is too strong — some B outside A might be C. Only I follows.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. Some [C] are not [B].
Conclusion I: Some [C] are not [A].
Conclusion II: Some [B] are [A].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: All A are B → all A are within B. Some C are not B → those C are outside B → they are outside A → Some C are not A (I valid). All A are B → Some B are A by conversion (II valid). Both follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. No [A] are [B].
2. All [B] are [C].
3. Some [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [D] are not [A].
Conclusion II: No [A] are [C].
Conclusion III: Some [C] are not [A].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: No A are B + All B are C → All B (not A) are C → Some C (which are B) are not A (III valid). Conclusion II: No A are C is NOT valid (A may be in C through other means). Conclusion I: Some D are not A — Some C are D, Some C are not A, but not all D are C, so I is not definite. Only III is definitely valid.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. All [A] are [C].
3. No [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: No [A] are [D].
Conclusion II: Some [B] are [C].
Conclusion III: Some [B] are not [D].
Which all follow?
templates.explanation: All A are C + No C are D → No A are D (I valid). Some A are B + All A are C → Some B are C (II valid). Some B are C + No C are D → Some B are not D (III valid). All three follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. All [C] are [D].
3. No [B] are [D].
Conclusion I: No [A] are [C].
Conclusion II: No [A] are [D].
Conclusion III: No [C] are [B].
Which all follow?
templates.explanation: No B are D + All A are B → No A are D (II valid). No B are D + All C are D → No C are B (III valid). No A are D + All C are D → No A are C (I valid). All three follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. All [B] are [C].
3. No [D] are [C].
Conclusion I: Some [A] are [C].
Conclusion II: No [D] are [B].
Conclusion III: Some [A] are not [D].
Which all follow?
templates.explanation: Some A are B + All B are C → Some A are C (I valid). No D are C + All B are C → No D are B (II valid). Some A are C + No D are C → Some A are not D (III valid). All three follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. Some [B] are [C].
3. All [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [A] are [D].
Conclusion II: Some [B] are [D].
Conclusion III: All [A] are [D].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: Some B are C + All C are D → Some B are D (II valid). All A are B — but the Some B that are D may not include A. So Conclusion I not valid. III is too strong. Only II follows.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. No [A] are [B].
2. Some [B] are [C].
3. All [A] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [C] are not [A].
Conclusion II: Some [D] are not [B].
Conclusion III: No [D] are [B].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: No A are B + Some B are C → Some C are B, and those C are not A → Some C are not A (I valid). All A are D + No A are B → Some D (which are A) are not B → Some D are not B (II valid). III (No D are B) too strong — not valid. I and II follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. No [B] are [C].
3. Some [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [A] are not [C].
Conclusion II: Some [D] are not [B].
Conclusion III: No [A] are [D].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: Some A are B + No B are C → Some A are not C (I valid). Some C are D + No B are C → Some D are C, and No B are C → Some D are not B (II valid). III (No A are D) too strong — not established. I and II follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. No [B] are [C].
3. Some [D] are [C].
Conclusion I: No [A] are [C].
Conclusion II: Some [D] are not [B].
Conclusion III: Some [D] are not [A].
Which all follow?
templates.explanation: All A are B + No B are C → No A are C (I valid). Some D are C + No B are C → Some D are not B (II valid). No A are C + Some D are C → Some D are not A (III valid). All three follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. Some [B] are [C].
3. No [C] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [A] are not [D] is a possibility.
Conclusion II: No [B] are [D].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: Some B are C + No C are D → Some B are not D. But II says No B are D which is too strong. Conclusion I (possibility) is valid. Only Conclusion I follows.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. All [B] are [C].
3. Some [A] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [D] are [C].
Conclusion II: Some [D] are [B].
Conclusion III: All [D] are [C].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: Some A are D + All A are B → Some D are B (II valid). Some D are B + All B are C → Some D are C (I valid). III All D are C is too strong. I and II follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. No [A] are [B].
2. Some [C] are [A].
3. All [D] are [B].
Conclusion I: No [D] are [A].
Conclusion II: Some [C] are not [B].
Conclusion III: All [C] are [A].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: No A are B + All D are B → No D are A → No A are D (I valid). Some C are A + No A are B → Some C are not B (II valid). III reverses Some C are A → not valid. I and II follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. Some [A] are [B].
2. All [C] are [B].
3. No [A] are [D].
Conclusion I: Some [B] are [A].
Conclusion II: Some [C] are not [D] is a possibility.
Conclusion III: No [B] are [D].
Which follow?
templates.explanation: Some A are B → Some B are A (I valid by conversion). Conclusion III No B are D is not established. Conclusion II (possibility) — No A are D, and C may or may not overlap A, so possibility of Some C not D is valid (II valid). I and II follow.

templates.pattern:
Statements:
1. All [A] are [B].
2. Some [B] are [C].
3. No [C] are [D].
4. Some [D] are [E].
Conclusion I: Some [B] are not [D].
Conclusion II: Some [E] are not [C].
Conclusion III: Some [A] are [C] is a possibility.
Which all follow?
templates.explanation: Some B are C + No C are D → Some B are not D (I valid). Some D are E + No C are D → Some E are D, and those are not C → Some E are not C (II valid). III is a possibility (Some A are C) since All A are B and Some B are C — it is possible. All three follow.
